nar.text: The engines were started one minute before the start during very fine drizzle and a wet track.
Caracciola from the third row darted in one of his lightning starts on the very left of the track, passing the leading trio before the South Turn.
At the end of the first lap, Caracciola passed the grandstand after 11m50s, five seconds ahead of Nuvolari's red Alfa Romeo.
Rosemeyer's car trails oil smoke; Brauchitsch gestures to his pit and Neubauer protests.
Caracciola skids into the embankment and damages a rear shock absorber; Nuvolari is two meters behind.
Severi retires with an oil pump problem.
At the end of the third lap Nuvolari had taken the lead, and passed the grandstand five seconds ahead of Caracciola with Rosemeyer four seconds further behind
After four laps Nuvolari had a lead of nine seconds over Rosemeyer, who had passed Caracciola, who was now four seconds behind.
Stuck stops over a minute with one cylinder bank dead and drops to second-last.
Caracciola comes slowly into the pits and retires with broken rear shock absorbers.
Martin overturns near Brünnchen, unhurt.
On lap five, midrace, the race pace increased since the drizzle had stopped and the circuit began to dry.
Rosemeyer laps in 11m25s to Nuvolari's 11m34s and is 100 meters behind at the line.
Rosemeyer passes Nuvolari for the lead.

On lap seven all of a sudden a light fog cover appeared and enveloped the circuit with clinging fog which caused every driver to slow down their pace except Rosemeyer who carried on relentlessly despite the ever denser fog.
Lang spins off in the fog, is pushed back by spectators and stops for rear tires; Brivio and Farina move up to third and fourth.
Visibility was down to around 50 meters.
Rosemeyer leads by almost a minute.
Brauchitsch retires with broken rear suspension after going into a ditch in the fog.
After nine laps Rosemeyer was leading Nuvolari by 1m40s.
Rosemeyer wins by over 2m13s from Nuvolari; Brivio and Farina follow.
